item.title: Escambia County Emergency Officials Credit Prior Disaster Experience for Faster Hurricane Response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County's emergency management team deployed lessons learned from previous disaster responses to speed up operations as Hurricane Isaias impacted the Florida Panhandle, according to Public Safety Director Eric Gilmore. Gilmore told InWeekly that sending county staff to assist with recovery efforts in other parts of Florida following recent…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County's emergency management team deployed lessons learned from previous disaster responses to speed up operations as Hurricane Isaias impacted the Florida Panhandle, according to Public Safety Director Eric Gilmore.

Gilmore told InWeekly that sending county staff to assist with recovery efforts in other parts of Florida following recent storms has significantly improved the department's readiness and coordination capabilities. The hands-on experience gained from those deployments has translated into sharper planning and faster mobilization when disasters strike locally.

The approach reflects a broader regional strategy where counties share resources and expertise during hurricanes and other emergencies, allowing emergency managers to anticipate challenges and streamline response protocols.

item.title: Escambia Schools Weighs Closing Lincoln Park, Warrington Elementary
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County School District is moving forward with plans to close Lincoln Park and Warrington elementary schools, prompting a community planning process that could reshape student attendance across the county. A student attendance zone committee met this week to tackle the practical logistics of the proposed closures. The Student…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County School District is moving forward with plans to close Lincoln Park and Warrington elementary schools, prompting a community planning process that could reshape student attendance across the county.

A student attendance zone committee met this week to tackle the practical logistics of the proposed closures. The Student Attendance Zone Advisory Committee (SAZAC) convened on October 6 to begin drafting new attendance zones that would direct students from both schools to other district facilities, according to InWeekly reporting.

The move is part of ongoing district efforts to address enrollment and facility needs across Escambia County schools. Details about the timeline for the closures and which schools would absorb students from Lincoln Park and Warrington have not yet been finalized. The advisory committee's recommendations will likely guide the district's next steps in the closure process.

item.title: ECUA Lifts Boil-Water Notice for All of Pensacola Beach
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA BEACH, Fla. — The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has lifted its precautionary boil-water notice for all of Pensacola Beach , marking another major step in the restoration of water service following Hurricane Isaias. ECUA announced the all-clear at 10 a.m. Wednesday after water-quality testing confirmed the system met applicable…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA BEACH, Fla. — The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has lifted its precautionary boil-water notice for all of Pensacola Beach, marking another major step in the restoration of water service following Hurricane Isaias.


ECUA announced the all-clear at 10 a.m. Wednesday after water-quality testing confirmed the system met applicable requirements.


Most mainland Escambia County customers and all customers on Perdido Key were cleared Tuesday.


A limited number of mainland addresses remain under separate precautionary boil-water notices.


Those customers should continue boiling tap water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and other consumption until ECUA specifically lifts the notice for their location.

Customers at remaining affected mainland addresses are being notified by ECUA.

The latest information is available through ECUA's official website.

item.title: GOP Primary Rival Backs Democrat Taddeo's Insurance Record in Florida CFO Race
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Republican who challenged Blaise Ingoglia for the GOP's Chief Financial Officer nomination earlier this year is now publicly praising Democrat Nikki Taddeo's record on insurance reform, marking the latest sign of bipartisan crossover in Florida's competitive CFO race. Dr. Frank Collige posted on Facebook this week that he is "ashamed" of the…
item.content:encoded:
A Republican who challenged Blaise Ingoglia for the GOP's Chief Financial Officer nomination earlier this year is now publicly praising Democrat Nikki Taddeo's record on insurance reform, marking the latest sign of bipartisan crossover in Florida's competitive CFO race.

Dr. Frank Collige posted on Facebook this week that he is "ashamed" of the current Republican CFO's voting record and sees in Taddeo "someone who has demonstrated a willingness to stand up for Floridians when it comes to insurance reform." Collige, a Republican, argued that insurance reform should transcend party lines and called for an independent CFO willing to hold insurance companies accountable. "My loyalty is to the people of Florida, not to a political party," he wrote.

The statement drew a sharp response from Florida GOP Chairman Evan Power, who suggested on X that Collige's primary challenge against Ingoglia was meant to divide Republicans. The endorsement also came as the GOP's newest attack ad against Taddeo appeared to backfire—critics noted the ad accused her of supporting legislation that Ingoglia himself voted for and Governor Ron DeSantis signed into law. The bill was authored by former Florida GOP Chairman Joe Gruters, now RNC Chairman.

Recent polling shows the race tight. Five public surveys have found Taddeo and Ingoglia tied or nearly even, with the latest from the conservative James Madison Institute putting both at 43 percent among likely voters, even as Republicans lead other statewide races by double digits. Taddeo's campaign is emphasizing affordability, government accountability, and property insurance—issues she says transcend partisan divides.

item.title: FPL Restoration Numbers Questioned After Holley Outages Persist
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Santa Rosa County business owner is raising questions about whether Florida Power & Light's reported power restoration figures accurately reflect the actual status of service in some areas, particularly after the recent hurricane-related outages. Gordon Goodin, who operates a business in Holley with two meters, told NewsRadio Pensacola that…
item.content:encoded:
A Santa Rosa County business owner is raising questions about whether Florida Power & Light's reported power restoration figures accurately reflect the actual status of service in some areas, particularly after the recent hurricane-related outages.

Gordon Goodin, who operates a business in Holley with two meters, told NewsRadio Pensacola that FPL's outage app shows his power restored, but his three-phase power line remains disconnected. He says a crew from Oklahoma told him Monday they couldn't restore service until tree-trimming was completed, then left without explanation Tuesday morning despite assessing the repair as "easy." The work required a new pole, about 100 feet of rewiring, and reconnection of the service jack—none of which has been completed as of Wednesday.

"The app says the report is still being analyzed," Goodin said, questioning whether contractors are inflating restoration numbers or whether FPL is aware of the discrepancy. He noted the problem appears widespread, citing friends in East Hill, Reservation Road, Bay Street, East Bay Boulevard, and other Holley locations reporting the same issue: the app shows power restored while they have no service.

NewsRadio Pensacola is investigating whether FPL's reported restoration numbers are accurate. The questions come as the utility continues recovery efforts across the region following recent hurricane damage.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Fire Rescue and EMS responded Monday to rescue a man who fell down an embankment along Scenic Highway, according to WKRG News 5.

The man fell approximately 25 feet down the steep embankment. Fire Rescue and EMS personnel coordinated the rescue operation to reach and extract the injured person from the difficult terrain.

Details on the man's condition and how the fall occurred were not immediately available. The incident underscores the terrain hazards along some of Escambia County's roadways and the capabilities of local emergency response teams in handling challenging rescue scenarios.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Fire Rescue prevented a home from being completely destroyed after responding to a structure fire on Mackey Drive on Tuesday afternoon. According to an ECFR Facebook post, firefighters arrived at the 2000 block of Mackey Drive and worked to contain and extinguish the blaze.

The fire was tied to recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias, according to WKRG News 5. Details on the exact cause and how recovery work may have contributed to the fire were not immediately detailed.

No information was provided on injuries or the extent of damage to the home. The quick response by county firefighters was credited with preventing the structure from being a total loss.

item.title: Warm, Sunny Weather Continues Through Thursday in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County area is tracking a pleasant stretch of weather before a weekend cool front moves in. Wednesday will be sunny with highs near 88 degrees and calm winds. Overnight, conditions remain clear with lows dropping to around 63. Thursday follows a similar pattern, with partly sunny skies gradually becoming sunny and highs near 86…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County area is tracking a pleasant stretch of weather before a weekend cool front moves in. Wednesday will be sunny with highs near 88 degrees and calm winds. Overnight, conditions remain clear with lows dropping to around 63.

Thursday follows a similar pattern, with partly sunny skies gradually becoming sunny and highs near 86 degrees. A light east wind around 5 mph is expected to develop. Thursday night will be mostly clear with lows again near 63.

The calm, dry conditions should make for comfortable outdoor activities, but residents should monitor forecasts for the cool front expected to arrive over the weekend.

item.title: Mysterious glowing plume lights up North Escambia skies before dawn
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The luminous display, which some observers described as resembling a giant jellyfish in space, was visible across the northern part of the county. Such phenomena…
item.content:encoded:
Early risers across North Escambia got an unusual treat Tuesday morning when a glowing, iridescent plume swept across the eastern horizon in the predawn hours, according to local reports.

The luminous display, which some observers described as resembling a giant jellyfish in space, was visible across the northern part of the county. Such phenomena are typically caused by rocket launches or debris reflecting sunlight at high altitude during twilight hours, when the sun illuminates objects in space while the ground remains dark.

No official confirmation has been released yet regarding the source of Tuesday's display. Anyone who witnessed the event is encouraged to report details to local authorities or astronomical groups who track such occurrences.

item.title: Visiting FFA Chapters Serve 700+ Meals to Storm-Hit Tate High Area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Two Florida FFA chapters rolled into the Tate High School area Tuesday with more than 700 hot meals, bringing comfort and fellowship to neighbors still recovering from recent storm damage in North Escambia County. The visiting agricultural students demonstrated the kind of cross-county solidarity that defines rural community response — showing up…
item.content:encoded:
Two Florida FFA chapters rolled into the Tate High School area Tuesday with more than 700 hot meals, bringing comfort and fellowship to neighbors still recovering from recent storm damage in North Escambia County.

The visiting agricultural students demonstrated the kind of cross-county solidarity that defines rural community response — showing up with food, labor, and a commitment to helping their peers rebuild. The effort underscores how young people in agriculture-focused programs see disaster recovery not as someone else's problem, but as a shared responsibility.

Tate High School and the surrounding Gonzalez area have been dealing with storm aftermath, and meals like these do more than fill bellies; they give families breathing room to focus on cleanup and repairs without worrying about cooking. The FFA chapters' willingness to travel and serve signals that mutual aid networks in Northwest Florida extend well beyond single counties when disaster strikes.

item.title: Hurricane Relief Event Set for Molino Wednesday Morning
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Residents in north Escambia County affected by Hurricane Isaias can access emergency support services Wednesday morning in Molino. The relief event begins at 9 a.m. at CrossFaith Church, 5701 Highway 29, and is being organized in partnership with ECUA Board Member Kevin Stephens and local volunteers. The event will offer shower pods and restroom…
item.content:encoded:
Residents in north Escambia County affected by Hurricane Isaias can access emergency support services Wednesday morning in Molino. The relief event begins at 9 a.m. at CrossFaith Church, 5701 Highway 29, and is being organized in partnership with ECUA Board Member Kevin Stephens and local volunteers.

The event will offer shower pods and restroom facilities for residents without utilities, along with charging stations to power phones and devices. Free supplies will include meals ready to eat (MREs), bottled water, cleaning supplies, and hygiene kits — all available while supplies last.

This is one of several relief initiatives underway across Escambia County as recovery efforts continue in the aftermath of the hurricane.

item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County School Board has extended school closures through October 19 due to storm damage and safety concerns, according to a report from Citizen Portal News Florida.

The decision comes after severe weather impacted the county, prompting the board to keep facilities shuttered beyond initial closure dates. Teachers and parents raised safety concerns that factored into the board's determination to maintain the closure.

No specific details on the extent of storm damage or which facilities were most heavily affected were immediately available. The closure affects all Santa Rosa County schools during the extended period.

A Gulf Shores business was destroyed in a fire early Tuesday morning, but the owner credits a nearby police officer with saving his life.

According to WKRG News 5, the fire broke out before dawn and quickly consumed the structure. The owner said he was fortunate to escape and attributes his survival to an officer who was on patrol in the area at the time.

Details about the cause of the fire, the specific business, and the extent of the officer's intervention were not immediately disclosed. Authorities have not yet released a damage estimate or indicated whether an investigation into the fire's origin is underway.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Okaloosa County is urging residents and visitors to stay out of beach water and public pools due to an increased risk of waterborne illness, according to WKRG-TV.

The advisory applies to both ocean and pool environments in the county. Health officials have not yet released specific details about the nature of the illness or the exact locations affected, but the warning suggests a situation serious enough to warrant public precaution.

Okaloosa County residents should monitor updates from the Florida Department of Health for more information on the duration of the warning and when it may be safe to resume normal water activities.

item.title: Escambia County cancels remaining 2026 neighborhood cleanups to focus on Hurricane Isaias recovery
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Neighborhood and Human Services has suspended all remaining neighborhood cleanup events this year as the department redirects resources toward Hurricane Isaias cleanup and recovery efforts throughout the county. Four scheduled cleanups have been canceled: Navy Point/Beach Haven on October 14, Northpointe on October 21, Olive Road…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Neighborhood and Human Services has suspended all remaining neighborhood cleanup events this year as the department redirects resources toward Hurricane Isaias cleanup and recovery efforts throughout the county.

Four scheduled cleanups have been canceled: Navy Point/Beach Haven on October 14, Northpointe on October 21, Olive Road on November 4, and Ensley North on November 18. The county said neighborhood cleanup programs will resume in 2027, with updates to be posted on MyEscambia.com.

Meanwhile, Escambia County is preparing to begin collection of storm-generated debris from Hurricane Isaias later this week. Residents should note that commercial debris will not be included in the county's pickup service. More information about the debris collection program is available on the county's website.

item.title: ECAT Resumes Service Wednesday With Route Changes Due to Storm Debris
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Area Transit will bring buses back on the road Wednesday, Oct. 14, but riders should expect some adjustments as crews work to clear storm debris from local streets. ECAT will operate normal service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit running 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not run at all due to impassable road…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Area Transit will bring buses back on the road Wednesday, Oct. 14, but riders should expect some adjustments as crews work to clear storm debris from local streets.

ECAT will operate normal service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit running 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not run at all due to impassable road conditions. On Route 51, Ensley Street will be skipped; riders needing that stop should board at Johnson Avenue and Vickie Street instead. The UWF trolleys also won't operate.

County officials warn that delays are likely across the system as cleanup continues. Commuters are advised to build extra time into their schedules. For questions, call ECAT at 850-595-3228.
